text:
amelia: quick follow-up from the multi-region residency rfc — i sketched a small hybrid precedence proposal and want quick opinions before i write it up formally. tl;dr: global default -> region tag -> tenant override; with a strict consent mask that can block cross-region writes for specific tenants. thoughts?

mike: generally +1 on hybrid. two quick q's: how does this interact with active/active KV cache ownership? if tenant override points to region B but kv ownership is in A, do we forward or proxy?

sophia: forwarding adds tail latency, proxying risks double-write windows. my preference would be: route-to-declared-region; if KV owner mismatch, do async-forward with sync-fallback only on high-consent tenants.

raj: agree w/ sophia. also we need to make the precedence computable at the proxy layer without hitting control plane on every request. that means include X-Residency-Decision header from auth/frontier service.

amelia: good point — proposal includes a residency header. sample precedence pseudocode i was thinking:

```
# compute residency target for request
if tenant_override: target = tenant_override
elif region_tag: target = region_tag
else: target = global_default
# consent mask check
if tenant_consent_mask.disallows(target): reject 403 or route to consented region
```

linda: for 403 vs fallback behavior, legal asked we default to the most private option (i.e., keep data in-region) rather than auto-redirecting. so in many cases we should reject and surface clear error to client. :warning:

mike: ok on default-to-reject for PII/consent. for performance-sensitive routes (chat generate) we might want a best-effort fallback that returns cached or degraded answers instead of error — dangerous but reduces uptime impact. maybe a per-route opt-in?

raj: per-route opt-in seems fine, but make it explicit in routing config and surfaced in console. also add telemetry: residency_decision, decision_reason, source_header. need to be able to audit where requests were served.

ops-bot: deploy reminder: residency-config-service v0.3 will roll tomorrow 03:00 UTC with header support. See <https://ci.redwood/1234|residency-config-service/pipeline>

amelia: thanks — timeline works. next steps i’ll: 1) add header spec + examples to rfc, 2) include explicit per-route opt-in boolean, 3) add operator playbook for reject vs fallback, 4) propose telemetry events.

sophia: add a small simulation to the rfc — random tenant overrides + region blackout for 24h to show failure modes and costs (forwarding, cache miss). last time that helped convince legal.

linda: can you also add suggested error codes and user-facing message text for SDKs? legal + support need consistent messaging.

amelia: will do. if no objections by EOD i’ll fold this into the follow-up doc and link to the operator checklist. thanks all. :raised_hands:
